title: Crowborough Debut Brings Best And Worst
title_candidates: Crowborough Debut Brings Best And Worst
Heathland Highs And Lows At Crowborough
A New Course Sorts The Field
theme: A maiden visit to a MacKenzie heathland exposes both brilliance and ruin in equal measure.
tone: Wry and precise, tracking triumph and calamity hole by hole.
opening_hook: Crowborough's high heathland turf offered panoramic views of the South Downs and, for at least one player, a ringside seat to his own collapse.

round_story.subject: Jon Baker follows his worst round of the TEG 4 Trophy so far with the best net score of the day at Crowborough, built around a four-hole purple patch either side of two closing quadruple bogeys.
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the best net-vs-par score anyone posts all round, a top-three finish in Jon Baker's own career on that measure, and it is what drags the TEG 4 Trophy race back level after Round 2 had threatened to put him adrift.
round_story.shape: Round 2 left Jon Baker with his worst round to date; at Crowborough he rattles off four pars in a row from the 11th to close within a shot of the outright net lead, then immediately drops quadruple bogeys at the 15th and 18th. Even with both blow-ups included, the round still nets out as the best net score of the day.
headline_candidates: From Nightmare To Best Of Day
round_story.standfirst: A four-hole purple patch bracketed by two quadruple bogeys somehow still added up to the best net score of the round.

race_story.subject: David Mullin's 17-gross round, the second-best gross round recorded in TEG history to date, blows the TEG 4 Green Jacket race wide open even as the TEG 4 Trophy tightens to a flat tie, while the TEG 4 Wooden Spoon changes hands from Stuart Neumann to Henry Meller.
race_story.why_it_matters: Three different races moved three different ways off the same day's play: David Mullin's Jacket cushion more than doubled, his Trophy lead evaporated entirely, and last place swapped occupants for the second time this tournament.
race_story.shape: David Mullin arrives with modest leads in both the Trophy and the Jacket; his near-record gross round balloons the Jacket gap to sixteen, but Jon Baker's response on the net scale draws the Trophy level at 8 apiece. Meanw.While Stuart Neumann briefly held the Spoon's bottom spot mid-round, Henry Meller's late collapse through the 13th to 15th hands him last place outright.
headline_candidates: Mullin's Big Day Reshapes Three Races
One Lead Grows While One Vanishes
race_story.standfirst: A near-record gross round for one man and a last-gasp collapse for another reshuffled all three competitions in a single afternoon.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams's outward nine at Crowborough contains four separate quadruple bogeys inside six holes, producing the third-worst gross round recorded in TEG history to date and his own second-worst round on both scales.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Four quadruple bogeys in a single round is a genuinely rare inventory of failure, and the resulting score sits in the bottom three all-time for gross and inside the worst two of his own TEG career.
discovered_storylines.shape: Gregg Williams opens with a double bogey at the 1st, then quadruple bogeys at the 2nd, 4th and 5th send him to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon reckoning before the round is a third done. A brief truce on the 16th and 17th offers no real recovery before a fourth quadruple bogey arrives at the 15th.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Three quadruple bogeys inside the first six holes were only the start of it.

race_state_note: The TEG 4 Trophy is level for the first time this tournament, while the Green Jacket gap has more than doubled and the Wooden Spoon has changed hands for the second time.
